**(ii) Evolution.** The time evolution of the model is the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),\qquad U(t+s)=U(t)U(s),\quad U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1},$$
defined by the spectral calculus of the self-adjoint generator ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]], [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]], [[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]). The energy unit enters the argument of the exponential so that $H_{\mathrm{op}}t/\hbar$ acts in the dimensionless spectral variable.

**(iii) State evolution.** A vector state evolves continuously, $\psi(t):=U(t)\psi(0)$ for every $\psi(0)\in H$, and the Schroedinger equation
$$i\hbar\,\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(t)$$
holds in the norm-differentiable sense exactly for initial vectors $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$, where the derivative is the norm limit of the difference quotients; for other vectors the equation is not asserted, although the evolution remains continuous. A density-operator preparation evolves as $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$, which is a density operator for every $t$ and satisfies $\operatorname{tr}\rho(t)=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

**(iv) Time-dependent families.** A prescribed time-dependent family $t\mapsto H(t)$ of self-adjoint operators is a different model assumption: a norm-continuous finite-dimensional Hermitian family is used only through the unitary two-time propagator that its family defines, and the exponential of the integral of $H(t)$ is not identified with that propagator unless the family commutes with itself at different times. The general unbounded time-dependent case requires a separate existence and domain theorem of its own and is not adopted by this postulate; the driven-dynamics page states its own assumptions for the models it treats.

**(v) Open systems.** A non-unitary evolution of the reduced description of a system coupled to an environment is an extension obtained from an explicitly chosen environment model and a declared reduction, not a replacement for clause (ii); no environment model is adopted by this postulate.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the isolated-system idealization. They assert nothing about the origin of the energy operator of a concrete system, about the accuracy of the idealization for a laboratory preparation, or about which laboratory interactions realize an isolated evolution; those are tested identifications in the sense of P7.

**(a) Assigned energy observable.** Adopt the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4) for a declared isolated system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned energy observable** of the system is an assigned sharp observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ in the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), whose declared unit $u_H$ is an energy unit in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] (joules in the SI conventions fixed there). Thus $H_{\mathrm{op}}:D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subset H\to H$ is densely defined and self-adjoint ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]), with spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ under the choice hypotheses of [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and its outcome law in a preparation is the law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). The assignment of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is part of the model specification, as in clause (i) of P4; this definition asserts nothing about which laboratory quantity of a concrete system realizes it.

**(b) The unitary flow.** The **time evolution** or **flow** of the isolated system is the family
$$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr):=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_H(\lambda)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P4 in the spectral calculus of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]); here $\hbar>0$ is the reduced Planck constant with its value and unit fixed by [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], so that $tH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ is dimensionless. Equivalently, $U(t)=e^{itT}$ for the self-adjoint generator $T:=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ with $D(T)=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$; the two readings agree by the uniqueness of the generator in Stone's theorem, and by [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]] ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]] clause (a)) the family $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group: $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$, $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]).

**(c) Schroedinger picture.** The **Schroedinger-picture evolution** of a preparation is fixed by clause (iii) of P4. A state vector evolves by $\psi(t):=U(t)\psi(0)$ for every $\psi(0)\in H$, and the **state at time $t$** of the pure preparation $[\psi(0)]$ is the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$, which is well defined because $U(t)$ is injective; a general preparation $\rho$, that is an element of the state space $D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], evolves by
$$\rho(t):=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*},$$
the reading of clause (iii) of P4 in the density-operator vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]). In this picture the assigned observables are held fixed at their assigned values and the preparation moves.

**(d) Heisenberg picture.** For a **bounded** assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ — that is, an assigned sharp observable with $A\in\mathcal B(H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]), so that $A$ is self-adjoint and everywhere defined — the **Heisenberg representative** of $(A,u_A)$ at time $t$ is the pair $(A_H(t),u_A)$ with the same declared unit and
$$A_H(t):=U(t)^{*}AU(t)=U(-t)AU(t).$$
By [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]] clauses (a) and (d), $A_H(t)$ is again bounded and self-adjoint with spectral projection-valued measure $E_{A_H(t)}(B)=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)$, so $(A_H(t),u_A)$ is again an assigned sharp observable of the framework; in this picture the preparation is held fixed at its value at time $0$ and the observables move. The two pictures are two bookkeeping devices for the same model; the statement that they assign the same outcome laws is proved in the Heisenberg-picture theorem of this page, not assumed here.

**(e) Stationary preparations.** A preparation $\rho\in D(H)$ is **stationary** for the assigned energy observable when $\rho(t)=\rho$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. A pure preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary when $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for every $t$, that is, when the evolved vector remains in the ray of $\psi$; the characterization of this condition by the eigenrays of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is proved in the stationary-states theorem of this page, not assumed here. An **energy eigenstate** is a pure preparation of a unit eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$, and a **stationary state** in the model is a stationary pure preparation; by that theorem the two notions coincide.

**(f) Energy-compatible observables.** An assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ is **compatible with the energy**, or **energy-compatible**, when its spectral projection-valued measure and that of the energy commute strongly,
$$E_A(B)E_H(C)=E_H(C)E_A(B)\qquad\text{for all Borel }B,C\subseteq\mathbb R .$$
This is an equality of bounded operators on $H$, not a relation between formal commutators on a small domain; the phrase **conserved quantity** for an energy-compatible assigned observable is a claim about the time invariance of its outcome law and is established in the energy-conservation theorem of this page for bounded $A$.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P4 together with P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P4, P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematics, assert no dynamics for a prescribed time-dependent family or for an open system (clauses (iv) and (v) of P4 are separate model assumptions treated on their own pages), assert no measurement model, no apparatus realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any laboratory system is exactly isolated.

**(a) Dimensions.** Write $\ell$, $\tau$, $\mu$, $\vartheta$ for the four independent dimension symbols of length, duration, mass and electric charge. A **dimension** is an element of $\mathbb Q^{4}$, written $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ with $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb Q$; products and inverses of dimensions are componentwise addition and negation, and the dimensionless dimension $\ell^{0}\tau^{0}\mu^{0}\vartheta^{0}$ is abbreviated $1$. The conventions assign to each quantity of the framework a dimension $[X]$, subject to $[XY]=[X][Y]$, $[X/Y]=[X][Y]^{-1}$ and $[dX/du]=[X][u]^{-1}$, with sums meaningful only between quantities of equal dimension, in which case the sum carries that dimension. For a rational power $q$, dimension powers mean $[X]^q=\ell^{qa}\tau^{qb}\mu^{qc}\vartheta^{qd}$ when $[X]=\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$. Rational exponents include the half-integer wave-function dimensions in clause (d); the integer-exponent dimensions form the subgroup $\mathbb Z^4$. These are consistency requirements on the conventions, not laws of nature.

For extensions using temperature, adjoin an independent dimension symbol $\Theta$: the enlarged group is $\mathbb Q^4\times\mathbb Q$, written $\ell^a\tau^b\mu^c\vartheta^d\Theta^e$, with the same componentwise rules. The preceding group embeds by $e=0$, so all previously assigned dimensions are preserved. Temperature has dimension $\Theta$, the Boltzmann constant has dimension $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-2}\Theta^{-1}$, and entropy in joules per kelvin has that same dimension; a dimensionless entropy remains dimensionless. This convention does not assign a temperature or an entropy to any system.

**(b) Reference units.** The **metre** (m), **second** (s), **kilogram** (kg) and **coulomb** (C) are the reference units of length, duration, mass and charge; a quantity of dimension $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ is expressed in the unit $\mathrm m^{a}\mathrm s^{b}\mathrm kg^{c}\mathrm C^{d}$. Coordinates of an inertial frame are read with the time coordinate $t$ in seconds, $[t]=\tau$, and the spatial coordinates $x_{i}$ in metres, $[x_{i}]=\ell$; slice distances of the arena are read in metres. In the temperature extension the reference unit of $\Theta$ is the kelvin (K), so the general reference unit gains a factor $\mathrm K^e$.

**(c) Defining constants of the current SI.** The framework keeps $\hbar$ explicit. In the current SI the constants $h$, $c$ and $e$ are exact defining constants, with the values $h=6{,}626\,070\,15\times10^{-34}$ J s, $c=2{,}99792458\times10^{8}$ m s$^{-1}$ and $e=1{,}602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}$ C, and $\hbar:=h/(2\pi)$. These are real scalar constants with dimensions and units $[h]=[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$ (J s), $[c]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ (m s$^{-1}$), and $[e]=\vartheta$ (C). The vacuum permeability $\mu_{0}$ is a positive real scalar that is experimentally determined in the current SI, with $[\mu_{0}]=\mu\ell\vartheta^{-2}$ (N A$^{-2}$ = H m$^{-1}$); $\varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1}$ is a positive real scalar with $[\varepsilon_{0}]=\mu^{-1}\ell^{-3}\tau^{2}\vartheta^{2}$ (F m$^{-1}$). These are unit-convention statements of the SI, not measurements reported by this framework; $c$ enters the framework only through the separate radiation assumptions adopted on their own pages, not in the nonrelativistic spacetime of [[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]].

**(d) Dimensions and types of the framework's quantities.** The dimension map is fixed on the following quantities.

1. State quantities: a position wave function of a system with $d$ spatial dimensions and $r$ internal components is an almost-everywhere equivalence class in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with dimension $\ell^{-d/2}$, its norm $\|\psi\|$ is dimensionless, and an abstract normalized state and the density operators of the state postulate are dimensionless.
2. Probability: the outcome probability $\mu(B)$ of the observable postulate is a dimensionless number; a position density $|\psi|^{2}$ has dimension $\ell^{-d}$; a momentum wave function normalized against $\mathrm d^{d}p$ has dimension $(\mu\ell\tau^{-1})^{-d/2}$; an amplitude for a finite outcome is a dimensionless complex number, while an amplitude read against a detector coordinate carries the square-root of the inverse of the detector measure.
3. Frame parameters ([[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]]): $[b]=\tau$, $[a_{i}]=\ell$, $[v_{i}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $[R_{ij}]=1$.
4. Mechanical quantities: action $[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; energy and the Hamiltonian eigenvalues $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$; momentum $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$; position components $\ell$; angular momentum and spin $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; mass $\mu$; velocity of a free spinless model $\ell\tau^{-1}$; force $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$; a real potential energy $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$.
5. Probability current: in the ordinary continuous-field regime, fix an integer $d\ge1$, an open spatial region $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ and an open time interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$. A **probability current density** is a declared continuous map $j:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^d$, whose spatial components have dimension $\ell^{1-d}\tau^{-1}$ and reference unit $\mathrm m^{1-d}\mathrm s^{-1}$. At fixed time it is a spatial vector field; its signed normal component is read as probability transported per unit spatial $(d-1)$-area and time. Explicitly, for a flat face $S=\{x:x_k=a,\ a_i\le x_i\le b_i\ (i\ne k)\}\subset\Omega$, with $a_i<b_i$ and chosen normal $n=\epsilon e_k$, $\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}$, define its **signed probability flux** at $t\in I$ as $\Phi_S(t):=\epsilon\int_{\prod_{i\ne k}[a_i,b_i]}j_k(x_1,\ldots,x_{k-1},a,x_{k+1},\ldots,x_d,t)\prod_{i\ne k}dx_i$. Here $e_k$ is the $k$th coordinate unit vector and the integral uses $(d-1)$-dimensional Lebesgue measure; for $d=1$ this means $\Phi_{\{a\}}(t)=\epsilon j(a,t)$. The flux has dimension $\tau^{-1}$ and unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$; positive sign means transport in the chosen normal direction. Fluxes through curved surfaces, or currents with weaker regularity, require separately specified surface measures or traces. This fixes the quantity type and flux convention; it supplies neither a current associated to an arbitrary $L^2$ state nor a conservation or detector law. Each dynamical model supplies its current construction and balance hypotheses.
6. Electric quantities of the model parameters: charge has dimension $\vartheta$; a magnetic moment has dimension $\ell^{2}\vartheta\tau^{-1}$, equivalently $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{2}=\mathrm J\,\mathrm T^{-1}$, and a gyromagnetic parameter $\gamma$ in the relation $\boldsymbol\mu=\gamma\mathbf S$ has dimension $\mu^{-1}\vartheta$, equivalently $\mathrm s^{-1}\mathrm T^{-1}$; these quantities appear only in the model assumptions that introduce them.
7. Statistical quantities: a mean has the dimension of its outcome coordinate, a variance the square of it and a standard deviation it; a mean, variance or higher moment exists only when the corresponding moment of the outcome probability is finite, so a symbolic average is not a number unless that integrability is established. Angles and phases are dimensionless under the radian convention.
8. Quantities of later extension assumptions - radiation frequencies and energies, electric dipole moments, cross sections, temperatures and entropies - are declared with their dimensions and units by the items that introduce those assumptions, under the rules fixed here; they are not part of the present list.

**(e) Conventions only.** No numerical value of any model parameter is fixed by this item: no mass, charge, spin label, potential or measured constant is asserted, and natural-unit shorthand (for example setting $\hbar=1$ or $c=1$) is read as an abbreviation for the corresponding SI-dimensioned statement with the constant restored.

derivations.claim:
[Pointwise continuity] For each $l$, the model equation holds almost everywhere and gives [given, F1, F2, algebra]
$$\partial_t\psi_l=\frac{i\hbar}{2m}\Delta\psi_l-\frac{i}{\hbar}V\psi_l.$$
By [F2],
$$\partial_t|\psi_l|^2=2\operatorname{Re}(\overline{\psi_l}\partial_t\psi_l)=-\frac{\hbar}{m}\operatorname{Im}(\overline{\psi_l}\Delta\psi_l),$$
because $V|\psi_l|^2$ is real almost everywhere. The product calculation in
[F2] also gives
$$\operatorname{div}j_l=\frac{\hbar}{m}\operatorname{Im}(\overline{\psi_l}\Delta\psi_l),$$
so $\partial_t|\psi_l|^2+\operatorname{div}j_l=0$ almost everywhere. This
left side is continuous on $\Omega\times I$ by the assumed regularity; if it
were nonzero at a point, continuity would make it nonzero on an open ball of
positive Lebesgue measure. It therefore vanishes everywhere. Summing the
finite number of component identities proves (a) and gives
$\partial_tn=-\operatorname{div}j$.

[Flow conservation] By [F6], $U(t)$ is unitary for every $t$, hence [given, F6, algebra]
$\|U(t)\psi_0\|=\|\psi_0\|$. For a unit vector the P2 position law therefore has total mass $\|U(t)\psi_0\|^2=1$ at every time. This proves (d).

[Integrated balance] Fix $t_0\in I$ and choose an open interval [given, step 1.1, F3, F4]
$J_0\subset I$ containing $t_0$ whose closure $J$ is a compact subset of $I$. Since $\overline D\times J$ is compact and $\partial_tn$ is continuous, it is bounded there; the constant bound on bounded $D$ is an integrable majorant. Applying [F4] on $J_0$ gives $\frac{d}{dt}\int_Dn=\int_D\partial_tn$ near $t_0$. By step 1.1 and [F3], this is $-\int_D\operatorname{div}j=-\int_{\partial D}j\cdot\nu\,dS$. Since $t_0$ was arbitrary, (b) holds on $I$.

[Global conservation] Assume the hypotheses of (c), and fix $s<t$ in [given, step 2.1, F5, algebra]
$I$. Since $I$ is an interval, $[s,t]\subset I$. For $R>0$ let
$B_R=\{x:|x|<R\}$ and $F_R(\tau)=\int_{B_R}n(x,\tau)dx$. By (b),
$$|F_R'(\tau)|=\left|\int_{\partial B_R}j\cdot\nu\,dS\right|\le\sum_{l=1}^r\int_{\partial B_R}|j_l|\,dS.$$
The mean value theorem in [F5] gives
$$|F_R(t)-F_R(s)|\le(t-s)\sum_{l=1}^r\sup_{\tau\in I}\int_{\partial B_R}|j_l(x,\tau)|dS,$$
whose right side tends to zero as $R\to\infty$. For each $\tau\in\{s,t\}$,
the balls increase to $\mathbb R^3$, so [F5] yields
$F_R(\tau)\to\int_{\mathbb R^3}n(x,\tau)dx$. The domination hypothesis makes
both limits finite. Letting $R\to\infty$ proves equality of the total
squared-amplitude integrals at $s$ and $t$. Since $s<t$ were arbitrary in $I$,
this integral is constant on $I$, proving (c).

[Conclusion and units] Steps 1.1, 2.1, 1.2 and 3.1 establish (a)-(d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2, step 3.1, F7, algebra]
The units in (e) follow from [F7]; its remaining sentences state the scope, and no detection law is identified with the flux.

boundaries.evidence: No empty index range arises: $r=2s+1ge1$ and all sums over components are nonempty; the integral balance of step 2.1 may be taken over an admissible region whose boundary is empty only if the region is empty, in which case both sides vanish.
Step 1.2 includes $psi_{0}=0$ (constant zero curve) and $psi_{0}$ unit; step 2.1 includes $V=0$ and $psiequiv0$.
Step 1.1 applies to each component, so the scalar case $r=1$ (spin $s=0$) is included, as is the one-dimensional potential with $V=0$.
Repeated or proportional components are summed componentwise in step 2.1 without any independence assumption; vanishing gradient or vanishing density is permitted.

Steps 1.1 and 2.1 evaluate the equation and the balance on the open sets $Omega$ and $I$ only, so endpoint differentiability is not asserted; the region $D$ of step 2.1 satisfies $overline DsubseteqOmega$, avoiding the boundary points of $Omega$.

Declared choice premises belong to P4/P5 and cited operator mathematics. Step 2.1 chooses a compactly contained neighborhood of the fixed t0 in the nonempty open interval I; step 1.2 uses the assigned unitary flow.

boundaries.reason: No clause of the statement is an if-and-only-if assertion: clauses (a)-(d) are one-directional identities, balance and conservation statements.
No converse is claimed: in particular clause (d) does not assert that a flow with constant norms must be the model's assigned unitary flow.

citations.quote:
Adopt the declared two-path preparation model of
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]], the
unsharp finite-outcome clause (iv) of the observable and probability postulate
P2, and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). The following vocabulary is used
by this page.

**(a) Declared recorded detector.** A **declared recorded detector** of the
arrangement is a finite set $A$ of **recorded outcome labels** with
$0\notin A$, together with measurable **recorded weights**
$w_{a}:\mathbb R^{3}\to[0,1]$ for $a\in A$ such that
$\sum_{a\in A}w_{a}(x)\le1$ for almost every $x\in\mathbb R^{3}$. The
**effect** of the label $a$ is the multiplication operator
$$F_{a}:=M_{w_{a}},\qquad (M_{w}\psi)(x):=w(x)\psi(x)\quad\text{a.e.},$$
on $H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, and the **no-record effect** is
$$F_{0}:=I-\sum_{a\in A}F_{a}.$$
The multiplier is a well-defined linear map on almost-everywhere classes,
since changing a representative on a null set changes its product only on
that null set.
Each $F_a$ is bounded: for $\psi\in H_s$,
$$\|M_{w_a}\psi\|^2=\int_{\mathbb R^3}w_a(x)^2\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^r}^2dx\le\|\psi\|^2,$$
so the boundedness inequality holds with bound $C=1$ by monotonicity of the
nonnegative integral ([[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]).
Thus $F_a$ is a bounded linear operator ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Because $w_a$
is real, the componentwise pairing gives
$\langle M_{w_a}\psi,\phi\rangle=\langle\psi,M_{w_a}\phi\rangle$ for all
$\psi,\phi\in H_s$; hence $F_a$ is self-adjoint by
[[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]. At almost every $x$, the finite-dimensional
operator $w_a(x)I_{\mathbb C^r}$ is nonnegative in the sense of
[[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]], and therefore
$$0\le\langle F_a\psi,\psi\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R^3}w_a(x)\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^r}^2dx\le\|\psi\|^2.$$
Here $0\le F_a\le I$ means these quadratic-form inequalities for every
$\psi\in H_s$.

Define $w_0(x):=\max\{0,1-\sum_{a\in A}w_a(x)\}$. This is measurable,
$0\le w_0\le1$, and it equals $1-\sum_aw_a$ almost everywhere by the
admissibility condition. Thus $F_0=M_{w_0}=I-\sum_aF_a$ on $H_s$, and the
same argument gives $0\le F_0\le I$ and self-adjointness. Consequently
$\sum_{a\in A}F_a+F_0=I$, so the completed family is a finite family of
bounded effects of clause (iv) of P2
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]).

**(b) Recorded probabilities.** For a preparation $\rho\in D(H_{s})$ the
**recorded probability** of a label $a\in A$ and the **no-record probability**
are
$$\nu(a):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho F_{a}\bigr),\qquad \nu(0):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho F_{0}\bigr)=1-\sum_{a\in A}\nu(a),$$
the outcome reading of clause (iv) of P2 for the declared effects
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (f)
records the reading; the numbers are nonnegative and sum to one). The
**recorded-event mass** is $\nu(A):=\sum_{a\in A}\nu(a)=1-\nu(0)\in[0,1]$. A
detector is **full-efficiency** when $\sum_{a}w_{a}=1$ almost everywhere, so
that $F_{0}=0$ and $\nu(0)=0$ for every preparation. For a fixed preparation
$\rho$, the model **loses** events when $\nu(0)>0$, and the no-record channel
carries this lost mass. A detector that is not full-efficiency can nevertheless
have $\nu(0)=0$ for a particular preparation. A **declared recorded bin** $B$ is
the special case with one label $a$ and $w_{a}=\mathbf 1_{B}$; then
$F_{a}=G(B)$ is the position projection of clause (e) of
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]], with the
position set $B$ read in the metre unit of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and the recorded probability is
the ideal bin probability.

**(c) Loss conditioning.** When $\nu(A)>0$, the **conditioned recorded law** is
$$\bar\nu(a):=\frac{\nu(a)}{\nu(A)}\qquad(a\in A).$$
It is a probability measure on the finite set $A$
([[def-probability-measure]]); it is the law of the recorded label under the
declared model conditioned on the occurrence of a record. Conditioning is a
statistical operation on the recorded data; it is not a state update, and no
claim of P3 is made here.

**(d) Sampling model.** A **declared $N$-trial sampling model** for a fixed
preparation $\rho$ is a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$
carrying measurable maps
$O_{1},\dots,O_{N}:(\Omega,\mathcal F)\to
(A\cup\{0\},\mathcal P(A\cup\{0\}))$ ($N\ge1$), where $0$ is the no-record
label of clause (b) and is distinct from every recorded label because
$0\notin A$. The maps are **mutually independent** in the sense of
[[def-independence-of-finite-random-variables]] and **identically distributed**
with $\mathbb P(O_{k}=a)=\nu(a)$ for every $a\in A$, $\mathbb P(O_{k}=0)=\nu(0)$
and every $k$, where $\nu$ is the recorded law of clause (b); the numbers
$\nu(a)$ and $\nu(0)$ sum to one, so this is a probability law on the finite
set $A\cup\{0\}$. The **empirical frequency** of the label $a$ in the sample is
$$F_{N}(a):=\frac{1}{N}\#\{k:O_{k}=a\}.$$
A **declared fringe criterion** for sample size $N$ is a subset
$C\subseteq(A\cup\{0\})^{N}$; the model **accepts** the sample when
$(O_{1},\dots,O_{N})\in C$ and **fails the criterion** otherwise. The
identification of repetitions of a concrete procedure with the independent
identically distributed model is an additional statistical assumption in the
sense of clause (ii) of P7; it is not a consequence of P1-P6, and correlated
trials, drifting preparation, dead time and selection must be modeled or
recorded as limitations if present ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

**(e) Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) fix the recorded-detector and sampling

A finite family of finite-valued random variables $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ is **mutually independent** when for every nonempty $J\subseteq I$ and every selection $x_j\in X_j(\Omega)$,
$$\mathbb P(X_j=x_j\text{ for every }j\in J)=\prod_{j\in J}\mathbb P(X_j=x_j).$$
It is **pairwise independent** when this identity is required only for two distinct indices. The empty family is mutually independent vacuously, and a one-member family is mutually independent.

Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a probability space.

- If $X:\Omega\to[0,+\infty]$ is measurable, its **expectation** is the
  extended-valued integral
  $$\mathbb E[X]:=\int_\Omega X\,d\mathbb P\in[0,+\infty].$$
- If $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ or $X:\Omega\to\mathbb C$ is integrable in the sense
  of [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]], its
  **expectation** is again
  $$\mathbb E[X]:=\int_\Omega X\,d\mathbb P,$$
  now a finite real or complex number.

For an integrable real random variable,
$$\mathbb E[X]=\mathbb E[X^+]-\mathbb E[X^-],$$
where $X^+$ and $X^-$ are its positive and negative parts.

Let $X,Y$ be integrable real or complex random variables on one probability
space.

1. For scalars $a,b$,
   $$\mathbb E[aX+bY]=a\,\mathbb E[X]+b\,\mathbb E[Y].$$
2. If $X$ and $Y$ are real-valued and $X\le Y$ almost surely, then
   $$\mathbb E[X]\le\mathbb E[Y].$$
3. $$|\mathbb E[X]|\le\mathbb E[|X|].$$

Let $X$ be a real random variable on a probability space.

- For $p>0$, the **$p$th absolute moment** of $X$ exists when $|X|^p$ is
  integrable, and is then
  $$\mathbb E[|X|^p].$$
- If $X$ is integrable, its **mean** is $\mathbb E[X]$.
- If $X$ is square-integrable, its **variance** is
  $$\operatorname{Var}(X):=\mathbb E[(X-\mathbb E[X])^2].$$

If $X$ and $Y$ are square-integrable real random variables on the same
probability space, their **covariance** is
$$\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y):=\mathbb E[(X-\mathbb E[X])(Y-\mathbb E[Y])].$$

If $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ is a finite pairwise-independent family, then
$$\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\sum_{i\in I}X_i\right)=\sum_{i\in I}\operatorname{Var}(X_i).$$
Pairwise independence, rather than mutual independence, is sufficient.

If $X$ is a square-integrable real random variable and $a>0$, then
$$\mathbb P(|X-\mathbb E[X]|\ge a)\le\frac{\operatorname{Var}(X)}{a^2}.$$

outcomes other than $a$ when an indicator is zero, gives

**(a) Framework data and state convention.** Adopt the state and composition
postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the kinematics and
one-particle model postulate P5, the identical-particle and spin postulate P6,
and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Fix a spin label
$s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$, put $r:=2s+1$, and fix a mass parameter
$m>0$. P5 assigns the one-particle state space
$$H_s:=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^r)$$
with almost-everywhere equivalence classes and pairing
$$\langle f,g\rangle:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\sum_{l=1}^r f_l(x)\overline{g_l(x)}\,dx,$$
linear in the first argument ([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). P1 identifies a pure
preparation with the ray $[\psi]:=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a
unit vector $\psi$ and a general preparation with a density operator, meaning a
bounded self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with
$\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[def-trace-class-operator]],
[[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). Write
$$D(H_s):=\{\rho:\rho\text{ is a bounded self-adjoint positive trace-class operator on }H_s\text{ and }\operatorname{tr}\rho=1\}$$
for the set of general preparations.

For a unit vector $u$, define $P_uf:=\langle f,u\rangle u$. By Cauchy--Schwarz
([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]),
$\|P_uf\|=|\langle f,u\rangle|\le\|f\|$, so $P_u$ is bounded. Then
$P_u^2=P_u$ and $P_u$ is self-adjoint because for $f,g\in H_s$,
$\langle P_uf,g\rangle=\langle f,u\rangle\langle u,g\rangle
=\langle f,P_ug\rangle$. Moreover
$\langle P_uf,f\rangle=|\langle f,u\rangle|^2\ge0$ by the inner-product
identities and $\langle u,u\rangle=1$. Its range is $\mathbb C u$, so it has
finite rank and is trace class by [[def-trace-class-operator]]. The one-term
nuclear representation $P_uf=\langle f,u\rangle u$ gives
$\operatorname{tr}P_u=\langle u,u\rangle=1$ by
[[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]. Thus $P_u$ is a
density operator. For $\psi\ne0$ define
$$\widehat\rho(\psi):=P_{\psi/\|\psi\|},\qquad \widehat\rho(\psi)f=\frac{\langle f,\psi\rangle\psi}{\|\psi\|^2}.$$
For every nonzero scalar $z$, conjugate-linearity in the second argument and
$\|z\psi\|^2=|z|^2\|\psi\|^2$ give
$$\widehat\rho(z\psi)f=\frac{\langle f,z\psi\rangle z\psi}{\|z\psi\|^2}=\frac{|z|^2\langle f,\psi\rangle\psi}{|z|^2\|\psi\|^2}=\widehat\rho(\psi)f,$$
so the pure density operator depends only on the ray.

**Position PVM and Born-density calculation.** P5 assigns the componentwise
position operators $Q_jf=x_jf$ on
$$D(Q_j):=\{f\in H_s:x_jf\in H_s\},\qquad j=1,2,3.$$
Each $Q_j$ is self-adjoint on this domain. To see density, for $f\in H_s$ put
$f_n=\mathbf 1_{\{|x_j|\le n\}}f$; then $f_n\in D(Q_j)$ and $f_n\to f$ in
$H_s$ by dominated convergence. If $f,g\in D(Q_j)$, then
$\langle Q_jf,g\rangle=\langle f,Q_jg\rangle$ because $x_j$ is real-valued
and both products are integrable by Cauchy--Schwarz. If $g\in D(Q_j^*)$ with
$Q_j^*g=h$, let $E_n=\{x:|x_j|\le n\}$. For every $q\in H_s$ supported in
$E_n$, one has $q\in D(Q_j)$ and
$\langle q,(x_jg-h)\mathbf 1_{E_n}\rangle=0$ by the defining adjoint
identity. The vector $(x_jg-h)\mathbf 1_{E_n}$ lies in $H_s$ because $x_j$
is bounded on $E_n$; taking it for $q$ shows $x_jg=h$ almost everywhere on
$E_n$. Since $E_n\uparrow\mathbb R^3$, $x_jg=h\in H_s$ almost everywhere,
so $g\in D(Q_j)$ and $Q_j^*g=Q_jg$. Symmetry gives the reverse domain
inclusion; hence $Q_j=Q_j^*$ by
[[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]].

For a Borel set $S\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, define the indicator multiplication
operator $M_{\mathbf 1_S}:H_s\to H_s$ by
$(M_{\mathbf 1_S}f)(x):=\mathbf 1_S(x)f(x)$ almost everywhere. This is
independent of the representative of the $L^2$ class and is bounded, since
$$\|M_{\mathbf 1_S}f\|^2=\int_S\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^r}^2dx\le\|f\|^2.$$
It is linear and a bounded operator with bound one
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). It is an orthogonal projection:
$\mathbf 1_S^2=\mathbf 1_S$ and the real indicator multiplier is
self-adjoint for the declared pairing.

For Borel $C\subseteq\mathbb R$, define
$$E_j(C):=M_{\mathbf 1_{\{x:x_j\in C\}}}.$$
Each value is a bounded orthogonal projection since
$\|\mathbf 1_{\{x:x_j\in C\}}f\|\le\|f\|$, and
$E_j(\varnothing)=0$,
$E_j(\mathbb R)=I$, and $E_j(C\cap D)=E_j(C)E_j(D)$. For a disjoint sequence
$(C_n)$ with union $C$, the squared norm of
$E_j(C)f-\sum_{n\le N}E_j(C_n)f$ equals
$$\int_{\{x:x_j\in C\setminus\cup_{n\le N}C_n\}}\|f(x)\|^2dx,$$
which tends to zero by dominated convergence; hence $E_j$ is strongly
countably additive. Its scalar measures are finite Borel measures
$$\langle E_j(C)f,f\rangle=\int_{\{x:x_j\in C\}}\|f(x)\|^2dx,$$
and are regular on $\mathbb R$ by
[[cor-second-countable-lch-locally-finite-borel-measures-are-regular]]. The
push-forward integral identity
$$\int_{\mathbb R}g(\lambda)d\langle E_j(\lambda)f,f\rangle =\int_{\mathbb R^3}g(x_j)\|f(x)\|^2dx$$
holds first for indicators and nonnegative simple functions and then for
nonnegative measurable $g$ by monotone convergence. In particular the domain
of $\int\lambda\,dE_j(\lambda)$ is exactly $D(Q_j)$ by the same identity
with $g(\lambda)=\lambda^2$. For bounded Borel $g$, the bounded PVM calculus
equals multiplication by $g(x_j)$: this holds for indicators by the
definition of $E_j$, for finite simple functions by linearity, and for bounded
Borel functions by uniform simple approximation and the norm bound of the
bounded calculus ([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]). Therefore the
truncations of the unbounded integral are multiplication by
$x_j\mathbf 1_{\{|x_j|\le n\}}$. For $f\in D(Q_j)$ these converge in $H_s$
to $x_jf$, since the squared tail norm is
$\int_{\{|x_j|>n\}}x_j^2\|f(x)\|^2dx\to0$ by dominated convergence. Thus
$\int\lambda\,dE_j(\lambda)=Q_j$ on exactly $D(Q_j)$, and the regular spectral
theorem identifies $E_j$ as the spectral PVM of $Q_j$
([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]],
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]).

Define the joint position PVM by
$$G(B):=M_{\mathbf 1_B}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R^3\text{ Borel}).$$
For each $f$, $\|G(B)f\|\le\|f\|$, so its values are bounded; indicator
multiplication gives its projection, identity, and intersection laws. Strong
countable additivity follows from dominated convergence applied to $\|f\|^2$.
Its scalar measures are $B\mapsto\int_B\|f(x)\|^2dx$, finite
regular Borel measures on $\mathbb R^3$. On coordinate rectangles,
$$G(C_1\times C_2\times C_3)=E_1(C_1)E_2(C_2)E_3(C_3).$$
The rectangles generate $\mathcal B(\mathbb R^3)$; the published Borel-product
and finite-measure uniqueness theorems show that these rectangle values
uniquely determine the joint PVM ([[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]],
[[lem-finite-measure-uniqueness-on-a-pi-system]],
[[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]): for any two candidate PVMs,
their finite scalar measures agree on the generating rectangles and on the
whole space, so they agree on every Borel set; the polarization identity in
the last lemma then gives equality of the operator values. This constructs the
mathematical joint position PVM; a physical joint detector reading is supplied
only for the finite effect families declared below. For a density operator
$\rho$ define
$\mu^G_\rho(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho G(B))$ for each Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$. Since $G$ is a PVM, this set function is a probability
measure by the general density/PVM calculation used in clause (ii) of P2. For a
finite Borel partition $(B_a)_{a=1}^m$,
the operators $G(B_a)$ are orthogonal projections and sum to $I$. For each
$f\in H_s$,
$\langle G(B_a)f,f\rangle=\|G(B_a)f\|^2\in[0,\|f\|^2]$, so they are
bounded effects with $0\le G(B_a)\le I$ in quadratic-form order. Clause (iv)
of P2 therefore assigns the channel probabilities
$p_a(\rho)=\mu^G_\rho(B_a)$; the two-channel partition
$(B,\mathbb R^3\setminus B)$ assigns $\mu^G_\rho(B)$ to bin $B$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]). Thus $G$ is the
mathematical joint position PVM, while the detector reading used here is the
declared finite-effect model of P2(iv); this does not assert that every three
sharp coordinate measurement is jointly realized by a laboratory apparatus.
For a unit vector $u$, the trace formula for the rank-one operator $P_u$ gives
$$\mu^G_{P_u}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(P_uG(B))=\|G(B)u\|^2=\int_B\|u(x)\|_{\mathbb C^r}^2dx,$$
and P7(iii) leaves identification of this ideal detector with a concrete
apparatus as a tested physical claim with uncertainty.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as required by
the cited trace and spectral suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Declared two-path assignment.** A **declared two-path preparation model**
of the apparatus is the assignment of two nonzero classes
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\in H_{s}$, called the **path components** of the model with
respect to the declared pair of alternative path conditions of the apparatus,
together with a declared **relative phase** $\varphi\in\mathbb R$ and a declared
**weight** $w\in[0,1]$. The assignment of $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}$, $\varphi$ and
$w$ is part of the preparation model in the sense of clause (i) of P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]): it is declared, not
computed from the framework, and no item of this page asserts that a particle
described by the model "took" one of the two paths.

**(c) Coherent preparation.** The declared two-path model is **admissible at
phase $\varphi$** when $\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\ne0$ in $H_{s}$. When it
is admissible, the **coherent preparation** of relative phase $\varphi$ is the
pure preparation
$$\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi):=\widehat\rho\bigl(\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\bigr),$$
the normalized rank-one density operator defined in clause (a). The relative
phase $\varphi$ is read in radians (dimensionless). Multiplying both path
components by one common nonzero scalar leaves their associated pure density
operator unchanged, while the declared relative phase remains part of the
preparation assignment.

**(d) Incoherent preparation.** For a declared weight $w\in[0,1]$ the
**incoherent preparation**, or **which-path preparation**, of the model is
$$\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w):=w\,\widehat\rho(\psi_{1})+(1-w)\,\widehat\rho(\psi_{2}).$$
It is a density operator: both summands are positive trace-class operators of
trace one; trace-class operators form a vector space, nonnegative real
combinations preserve positivity and self-adjointness, and the trace is linear,
so $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w)=w+(1-w)=1$
([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]],
[[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). The weight $w$
is a declared preparation weight, not an outcome probability.

**(e) Ideal detection bins.** A **declared ideal detector** of the model is a
finite family $\mathcal B=(B_{a})_{a=1}^{m}$ of pairwise disjoint Borel subsets
of $\mathbb R^{3}$ with $\bigcup_{a}B_{a}=\mathbb R^{3}$; the **ideal bin
probabilities** of a preparation $\rho\in D(H_{s})$ are the numbers
$$p_{a}(\rho):=\mu^{G}_{\rho}(B_{a})=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,G(B_{a})\bigr)\qquad(a=1,\dots,m),$$
the reading of the finite-effect clause (iv) of P2 for the declared detector
and its mathematical joint position PVM
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]). By clause (iv) of P2 these numbers are
nonnegative, are at most one, and satisfy
$\sum_{a}p_{a}(\rho)=1$. A single **declared bin** $B$ is the two-element ideal
detector $(B,\mathbb R^{3}\setminus B)$; its probability is $\mu^{G}_{\rho}(B)$.

For the **ideal support**, choose a Lebesgue-measurable representative $f$ of
the unit $L^2$ class and form $S_f:=\{x:\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^r}>0\}$. The
ideal support is the class of $S_f$ under equality up to a Lebesgue-null
symmetric difference. This class is independent of the representative, and
it is not asserted to be a Borel detector bin.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the model data of the pair:
the framework reading, the declared path components and preparations, and the
ideal bin reading of the position observable. They adopt no assumption beyond
P1, P2, P5, P6, P7 and the cited mathematics; the declaration of
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2},\varphi,w$ and of the bins is an apparatus-model input, and
the claim that a concrete two-slit apparatus realizes a particular such
declaration is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7(iii). The
declared bins are subsets of $\mathbb R^{3}$; the model does not claim that a
physical screen of lower dimension is literally a spatial region, and a
marginal, coarse-graining or flux reduction of a state to a screen coordinate
or surface is a separate detection model, not supplied here. No dynamics, no
recorded-event response, no sampling model and no empirical result is
asserted; the recorded-event and sampling models are declared separately on
this page.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following statements about sharp and unsharp real-valued quantities. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The latter is the explicit hypothesis used to obtain the spectral PVM of a general self-adjoint operator from [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] in clause (ii); consumers invoking this construction inherit it.

**(i) Sharp observables.** An **ideal sharp real-valued quantity** (observable) of a system with state space $H$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), meaning $D(A)=D(A^*)$ and $A\psi=A^*\psi$ on this common domain, together with a declared unit in which its real spectral coordinate is read; the unit is part of the assignment, and no numerical value of the coordinate is asserted by the assignment. Symmetry of $A$ on a small domain is not sufficient for self-adjointness, and the domain is a declared part of the observable.

**(ii) Spectral probability.** Let $E_{A}$ be the spectral projection-valued measure of the self-adjoint operator $A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$ and a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ the **probability of the outcome in $B$** is
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_{A}(B)\bigr),\qquad\text{and for a pure preparation }[\psi]\text{ it is }\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}.$$
By clause (b) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] the assignment $B\mapsto\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$ is a probability measure on the Borel sets ([[def-probability-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). It is the general form of the Born rule adopted here.

**(iii) Nature of the outcome law.** The probability law is a measure, not necessarily a density with respect to Lebesgue measure and not necessarily a finite or countable sum of point masses: a self-adjoint operator with continuous spectrum ordinarily has no normalizable eigenvector at a point of its continuous spectrum, so an "exact value" of a continuum quantity is not represented by a normalized state. An ideal point value is an idealization; a real detector reports a finite-resolution outcome, that is, the probability of a declared Borel set $B$ such as a bin, and the recorded-event probability is that of (ii) for the bin, not the value of a density at a point.

**(iv) Unsharp finite outcomes.** Outcomes of a finite-resolution apparatus with finitely many channels are described, when the idealization uses bounded effects, by a finite family $(F_{a})_{a=1}^{p}$ of effects on $H$ as defined above, with $\sum_aF_a=I$. The **outcome probabilities** are $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$. They are normalized for every state space assigned by P1, as shown by the preceding general-$H$ calculation. This unsharp extension is an operational description tied to an apparatus model; it is not obtained from the sharp observable by mathematical manipulation alone, and the effects alone do not determine what happens to the state after the outcome (P3).

**(v) Moments are a separate matter.** Statements about the mean, variance or higher moments of the outcome law require the corresponding integrability of $t\mapsto t^{n}$ against $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ and are not part of this postulate; where they are used they are stated with their hypotheses. In particular the existence of $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$ for an unbounded $A$ is not asserted.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model. They assert nothing about which quantities of a concrete apparatus are sharp, about the physical mechanism producing an outcome or about the completeness of the description; a laboratory record is a classical event whose relation to the model is a tested identification with uncertainty, in the sense of P7.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space.

- For $0<p<\infty$, define an equivalence relation on $\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ by
  $$f\sim g\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f-g\in\mathcal N(\mu),$$
  and write $L^p(\mu)$ for the set of classes $[f]$.
- For $p=\infty$, define the same relation on $L^\infty(\mu)$ and again write
  $L^\infty(\mu)$ for the set of classes.

Thus an element of $L^p(\mu)$ is an almost-everywhere equivalence class of
measurable representatives.

When $1\le p\le\infty$, the displayed set quotient agrees with the usual
quotient-vector-space construction of
[[def-quotient-vector-space-and-canonical-projection]].

For $0<p<1$, the same class notation is used; under its stated choice hypothesis, the later item
[[thm-the-l-p-distance-for-zero-less-p-less-one-is-a-complete-translation-invariant-metric]]
supplies the metric structure rather than a normed-space structure.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to [0,\infty]$ be product-measurable. Then
$x \mapsto \int_Y f_x\,d\nu$ and $y \mapsto \int_X f^y\,d\mu$ are measurable,
and

$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

Let $n \ge 1$, **assume the Axiom of Countable Choice**
([[def-countable-choice]]), and let $a_i \le b_i$ be reals for $i<n$. Write

$$R^{\circ} := \{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^n : a_i < x_i < b_i \text{ for every } i<n \,\}, \qquad \overline{R} := [a,b] = \{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^n : a_i \le x_i \le b_i \text{ for every } i<n \,\}$$

([[def-multidimensional-rectangle-and-volume]]). Then $R^{\circ}$ is open and
$\overline{R}$ is closed, so both are Borel and Lebesgue measurable, and **every**
set $R$ with $R^{\circ} \subseteq R \subseteq \overline{R}$ is Lebesgue
measurable with

$$\lambda_n(R) \;=\; \prod_{i<n}(b_i-a_i).$$

In particular this covers the four one-dimensional face conventions in each
coordinate — the open box, the closed box $[a,b]$, the half-open box
$B(a,b) = \prod_{i<n}(a_i,b_i]$ of [[def-half-open-box]], and every mixture of
them, in any combination of coordinates — and it gives measure $0$ to all of them
whenever $a_i = b_i$ for some $i<n$. For a half-open box with infinite
parameters the value is already
$\lambda_n(B) = \operatorname{vol}(B)$ ([[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-complete-measure]]).

Let $s=\sum_{j=1}^m c_j\chi_{E_j}$ be a simple representation of a
nonnegative simple measurable function
([[def-nonnegative-simple-measurable-function]]) on a measure space
$(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$, so the $E_j\in\mathcal A$ are pairwise disjoint and
$c_j\ge0$. Its
**simple integral** is
$$\int s\,d\mu:=\sum_{j=1}^m c_j\mu(E_j),$$
where $\mu$ is the given measure ([[def-measure]]) and the convention
$0\cdot(+\infty)=0$ is fixed once and for all.

The next lemma proves that this value is independent of the chosen simple
representation.

If $f,g:X\to[0,+\infty]$ are measurable, then
$$\int(f+g)\,d\mu=\int f\,d\mu+\int g\,d\mu.$$

Let $m,n \ge 1$. Under the identification
$$\mathbb R^{m+n}=\mathbb R^m \times \mathbb R^n,$$
one has
$$\mathcal B(\mathbb R^m)\otimes\mathcal B(\mathbb R^n) = \mathcal B(\mathbb R^{m+n}).$$

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces. Then:

1. the set function $E \mapsto (\mu \times \nu)(E)$ of
   [[def-product-measure-on-sigma-finite-spaces]] is a measure on
   $\mathcal A \otimes \mathcal B$;
2. for measurable rectangles,
   $$(\mu \times \nu)(A \times B)=\mu(A)\nu(B),$$
   with the nonnegative extended-product convention $0\cdot\infty=\infty\cdot0=0$;
3. the measure $\mu \times \nu$ is sigma-finite; and
4. it is the unique measure on $\mathcal A \otimes \mathcal B$ with the
   rectangle formula.

Let $n\in\mathbb N$ with $n\ge1$. In the product topology on $\mathbb R^n$,
each of the following families generates $\mathcal B(\mathbb R^n)$: all open
sets; all closed sets; all compact sets; all Euclidean open balls; all open
boxes; all rational open boxes; and all rational half-open boxes
$\prod_{i<n}(a_i,b_i]$ with rational endpoints $a_i<b_i$.

Let $\mathcal P$ be a pi-system on $X$ generating $\mathcal A$, and let $\mu,\nu$ be measures on $(X,\mathcal A)$ that agree on $\mathcal P$. Suppose there is an increasing sequence $(P_n)$ in $\mathcal P$ with

$$X=\bigcup_nP_n,\qquad \mu(P_n)=\nu(P_n)<+\infty\quad(n\in\mathbb N).$$

Then $\mu=\nu$ on $\mathcal A$.

Let $n \ge 1$ and **assume the Axiom of Countable Choice**
([[def-countable-choice]]). Write $\beta_n$ for the restriction of $\lambda_n$ to
the Borel sigma-algebra $\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^n)$
([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). Then $\mathcal{L}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is exactly the
completion domain of $(\mathbb{R}^n, \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^n), \beta_n)$
([[def-completion-of-a-measure-space]]), and $\lambda_n$ is the completed measure
there. Explicitly,

$$E \in \mathcal{L}(\mathbb{R}^n) \iff E = A\cup N \text{ for some } A, Z \in \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^n) \text{ with } N \subseteq Z \text{ and } \beta_n(Z) = 0,$$

and then $\lambda_n(E) = \beta_n(A)$.

derivations.claim: [Product-form norms] By [L4], the Lebesgue integral on $\mathbb R^3$ of these product functions is the product-measure integral. Thus, for $j=1,2$, Tonelli and $\|g\|=1$, $\|f_{j}\|^{2}=|I_{j}|/L=1$ give $\|\psi_{j}\|^{2}=\int_{\mathbb R}\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}|f_{j}(x_{1})|^{2}|g(x_{2},x_{3})|^{2}d(x_{2},x_{3})dx_{1}=\|f_{j}\|^{2}\|g\|^{2}=1\cdot1=1$, so $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}$ are nonzero unit classes. Since $f_{1}=L^{-1/2}$ on $I_{1}\setminus I_{2}$, a set of length $d>0$, one has $f_{1}+e^{i\varphi}f_{2}\ne0$ for every $\varphi$.

[Densities] On $O$ both indicators equal one, so $|f_{1}+e^{i\varphi}f_{2}|^{2}=\frac{|1+e^{i\varphi}|^{2}}{L}=\frac{2(1+\cos\varphi)}{L}$; on $I_{1}\setminus I_{2}$ only $f_{1}$ contributes, giving $\frac1L$, and symmetrically on $I_{2}\setminus I_{1}$; outside $I_{1}\cup I_{2}$ both vanish. Integrating over $\mathbb R$ gives $\|f_{1}+e^{i\varphi}f_{2}\|^{2}=\frac{2(1+\cos\varphi)(L-d)}{L}+\frac{2d}{L}=2+\frac{2(L-d)\cos\varphi}{L}=N_{\varphi}$, so the model is admissible at every phase.

[Slab laws] Write $\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}=(f_{1}+e^{i\varphi}f_{2})g$ and $|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}|^{2}=|f_{1}+e^{i\varphi}f_{2}|^{2}|g|^{2}$; by [L4] and Tonelli over $B_{1}\times\mathbb R^{2}$, $\int_{B_{1}\times\mathbb R^{2}}|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}|^{2}d(x_{1},x_{2},x_{3})=\bigl(\int_{B_{1}}|f_{1}+e^{i\varphi}f_{2}|^{2}dx\bigr)\|g\|^{2}=\int_{B_{1}}|f_{1}+e^{i\varphi}f_{2}|^{2}dx$, and likewise $\int_{B_{1}\times\mathbb R^{2}}|\psi_{j}|^{2}=\int_{B_{1}}|f_{j}|^{2}dx=|B_{1}\cap I_{j}|/L$; substituting into [L1] gives the two displayed laws of (b).

[Overlap, outer and dark values] Using the density values of step 2.1 and additivity of the integral, $\int_{O}|f_{1}+e^{i\varphi}f_{2}|^{2}dx=\frac{2(1+\cos\varphi)(L-d)}{L}$ and $\int_{I_{j}\setminus I_{3-j}}|f_{1}+e^{i\varphi}f_{2}|^{2}dx=\frac dL$, so the coherent values of (c) follow after dividing by $N_{\varphi}=2+\frac{2(L-d)\cos\varphi}{L}$: for the overlap, $\frac{2(1+\cos\varphi)(L-d)/L}{2(L+(L-d)\cos\varphi)/L}=\frac{(L-d)(1+\cos\varphi)}{L+(L-d)\cos\varphi}$, and for each outer region $\frac{d/L}{2(L+(L-d)\cos\varphi)/L}=\frac{d}{2L+2(L-d)\cos\varphi}$; the two outer values and the overlap value sum to one. The which-path values follow from $|B_{1}\cap I_{j}|/L$ with $w=\frac12$ and $|O|=L-d$, $|I_{j}\setminus I_{3-j}|=d$. At $\varphi=\pi$ the coherent overlap value is zero, the outer values are $d/(2L-2(L-d))=\frac12$ each, and the which-path overlap value is $\frac{L-d}{L}>0$ because $L>d$; a bin contained in $O$ has $|B_{1}\cap I_{1}|=|B_{1}\cap I_{2}|=|B_{1}|$ and coherent density zero there, while a bin meeting an outer region in a set of positive length meets $\{f_{1}+e^{i\varphi}f_{2}\ne0\}$ in a set of positive length, so its coherent probability is positive; the which-path positivity for bins meeting $O$ follows from $\frac12|B_{1}\cap I_{1}|/L>0$. This proves (c) and (d).

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the
internal-factor postulate P6, as read by
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]], and the
preparation and apparatus discipline P7, and adopt the declared two-path
preparation model of that definition with path components
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\in H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, relative phase
$\varphi\in\mathbb R$ and weight $w\in[0,1]$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}}$ be the joint position
PVM constructed in clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]], and read
its outcome law by P2 as $\mu^{G}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho G(B))$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]). Put
$$N:=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2},\qquad Z(B):=\int_{B}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}dx,\qquad Z:=Z(\mathbb R^{3}),\qquad c(B):=\operatorname{Re}Z(B),\qquad c:=c(\mathbb R^{3}).$$
Then:

(a) *Coherent law.* If the declared model is admissible at phase $\varphi$,
then for every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$
$$\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi)}(B)=\frac{\displaystyle\int_{B}\|\psi_{1}(x)+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx}{\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\|^{2}} ,$$
and the numerator expands as
$$\int_{B}\bigl(\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}\bigr)dx+2\operatorname{Re}\Bigl(e^{-i\varphi}\int_{B}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}dx\Bigr),$$
with denominator $N+2\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\varphi}Z)$; in particular
$\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\|^{2}>0$.

(b) *Which-path law.* For the declared weight $w\in[0,1]$ and every Borel set
$B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$,
$$\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w)}(B)=w\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_{B}\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}\,dx}{\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}}+(1-w)\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_{B}\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}\,dx}{\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}} .$$

(c) *Coincidence criterion.* Let $w_{*}:=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}/N$, so that
$\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w_{*})}(B)=N^{-1}\int_{B}(\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2})dx$.
If the declared model is admissible at phase $0$, then
$\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(0)}(B)=\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w_{*})}(B)$
for every Borel set $B$ if and only if
$$N\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=c\,\bigl(\|\psi_{1}(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}+\|\psi_{2}(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\bigr)\qquad\text{for almost every }x .$$
In particular, if $\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=0$ for
almost every $x$, then the coherent law of phase $0$ and the which-path law of
weight $w_{*}$ agree on every bin; and if $c=0$, then, under phase-$0$
admissibility, they agree if and only if
$\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=0$ for
almost every $x$.

(d) *Scope.* Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional on P1, P2, P5, P6 and the
declared model, and identify the laws of exactly two declared preparations.
They assert no path ontology, use no entangled marker state and no reduced

**(a) Framework data and state convention.** Adopt the state and composition
postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the kinematics and
one-particle model postulate P5, the identical-particle and spin postulate P6,
and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Fix a spin label
$s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$, put $r:=2s+1$, and fix a mass parameter
$m>0$. P5 assigns the one-particle state space
$$H_s:=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^r)$$
with almost-everywhere equivalence classes and pairing
$$\langle f,g\rangle:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\sum_{l=1}^r f_l(x)\overline{g_l(x)}\,dx,$$
linear in the first argument ([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). P1 identifies a pure
preparation with the ray $[\psi]:=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a
unit vector $\psi$ and a general preparation with a density operator, meaning a
bounded self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with
$\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[def-trace-class-operator]],
[[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). Write
$$D(H_s):=\{\rho:\rho\text{ is a bounded self-adjoint positive trace-class operator on }H_s\text{ and }\operatorname{tr}\rho=1\}$$
for the set of general preparations.

For a unit vector $u$, define $P_uf:=\langle f,u\rangle u$. By Cauchy--Schwarz
([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]),
$\|P_uf\|=|\langle f,u\rangle|\le\|f\|$, so $P_u$ is bounded. Then
$P_u^2=P_u$ and $P_u$ is self-adjoint because for $f,g\in H_s$,
$\langle P_uf,g\rangle=\langle f,u\rangle\langle u,g\rangle
=\langle f,P_ug\rangle$. Moreover
$\langle P_uf,f\rangle=|\langle f,u\rangle|^2\ge0$ by the inner-product
identities and $\langle u,u\rangle=1$. Its range is $\mathbb C u$, so it has
finite rank and is trace class by [[def-trace-class-operator]]. The one-term
nuclear representation $P_uf=\langle f,u\rangle u$ gives
$\operatorname{tr}P_u=\langle u,u\rangle=1$ by
[[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]. Thus $P_u$ is a
density operator. For $\psi\ne0$ define
$$\widehat\rho(\psi):=P_{\psi/\|\psi\|},\qquad \widehat\rho(\psi)f=\frac{\langle f,\psi\rangle\psi}{\|\psi\|^2}.$$
For every nonzero scalar $z$, conjugate-linearity in the second argument and
$\|z\psi\|^2=|z|^2\|\psi\|^2$ give
$$\widehat\rho(z\psi)f=\frac{\langle f,z\psi\rangle z\psi}{\|z\psi\|^2}=\frac{|z|^2\langle f,\psi\rangle\psi}{|z|^2\|\psi\|^2}=\widehat\rho(\psi)f,$$
so the pure density operator depends only on the ray.

**Position PVM and Born-density calculation.** P5 assigns the componentwise
position operators $Q_jf=x_jf$ on
$$D(Q_j):=\{f\in H_s:x_jf\in H_s\},\qquad j=1,2,3.$$
Each $Q_j$ is self-adjoint on this domain. To see density, for $f\in H_s$ put
$f_n=\mathbf 1_{\{|x_j|\le n\}}f$; then $f_n\in D(Q_j)$ and $f_n\to f$ in
$H_s$ by dominated convergence. If $f,g\in D(Q_j)$, then
$\langle Q_jf,g\rangle=\langle f,Q_jg\rangle$ because $x_j$ is real-valued
and both products are integrable by Cauchy--Schwarz. If $g\in D(Q_j^*)$ with
$Q_j^*g=h$, let $E_n=\{x:|x_j|\le n\}$. For every $q\in H_s$ supported in
$E_n$, one has $q\in D(Q_j)$ and
$\langle q,(x_jg-h)\mathbf 1_{E_n}\rangle=0$ by the defining adjoint
identity. The vector $(x_jg-h)\mathbf 1_{E_n}$ lies in $H_s$ because $x_j$
is bounded on $E_n$; taking it for $q$ shows $x_jg=h$ almost everywhere on
$E_n$. Since $E_n\uparrow\mathbb R^3$, $x_jg=h\in H_s$ almost everywhere,
so $g\in D(Q_j)$ and $Q_j^*g=Q_jg$. Symmetry gives the reverse domain
inclusion; hence $Q_j=Q_j^*$ by
[[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]].

For a Borel set $S\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, define the indicator multiplication
operator $M_{\mathbf 1_S}:H_s\to H_s$ by
$(M_{\mathbf 1_S}f)(x):=\mathbf 1_S(x)f(x)$ almost everywhere. This is
independent of the representative of the $L^2$ class and is bounded, since
$$\|M_{\mathbf 1_S}f\|^2=\int_S\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^r}^2dx\le\|f\|^2.$$
It is linear and a bounded operator with bound one
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). It is an orthogonal projection:
$\mathbf 1_S^2=\mathbf 1_S$ and the real indicator multiplier is
self-adjoint for the declared pairing.

For Borel $C\subseteq\mathbb R$, define
$$E_j(C):=M_{\mathbf 1_{\{x:x_j\in C\}}}.$$
Each value is a bounded orthogonal projection since
$\|\mathbf 1_{\{x:x_j\in C\}}f\|\le\|f\|$, and
$E_j(\varnothing)=0$,
$E_j(\mathbb R)=I$, and $E_j(C\cap D)=E_j(C)E_j(D)$. For a disjoint sequence
$(C_n)$ with union $C$, the squared norm of
$E_j(C)f-\sum_{n\le N}E_j(C_n)f$ equals
$$\int_{\{x:x_j\in C\setminus\cup_{n\le N}C_n\}}\|f(x)\|^2dx,$$
which tends to zero by dominated convergence; hence $E_j$ is strongly
countably additive. Its scalar measures are finite Borel measures
$$\langle E_j(C)f,f\rangle=\int_{\{x:x_j\in C\}}\|f(x)\|^2dx,$$
and are regular on $\mathbb R$ by
[[cor-second-countable-lch-locally-finite-borel-measures-are-regular]]. The
push-forward integral identity
$$\int_{\mathbb R}g(\lambda)d\langle E_j(\lambda)f,f\rangle =\int_{\mathbb R^3}g(x_j)\|f(x)\|^2dx$$
holds first for indicators and nonnegative simple functions and then for
nonnegative measurable $g$ by monotone convergence. In particular the domain
of $\int\lambda\,dE_j(\lambda)$ is exactly $D(Q_j)$ by the same identity
with $g(\lambda)=\lambda^2$. For bounded Borel $g$, the bounded PVM calculus
equals multiplication by $g(x_j)$: this holds for indicators by the
definition of $E_j$, for finite simple functions by linearity, and for bounded
Borel functions by uniform simple approximation and the norm bound of the
bounded calculus ([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]). Therefore the
truncations of the unbounded integral are multiplication by
$x_j\mathbf 1_{\{|x_j|\le n\}}$. For $f\in D(Q_j)$ these converge in $H_s$
to $x_jf$, since the squared tail norm is
$\int_{\{|x_j|>n\}}x_j^2\|f(x)\|^2dx\to0$ by dominated convergence. Thus
$\int\lambda\,dE_j(\lambda)=Q_j$ on exactly $D(Q_j)$, and the regular spectral
theorem identifies $E_j$ as the spectral PVM of $Q_j$
([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]],
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]).

Define the joint position PVM by
$$G(B):=M_{\mathbf 1_B}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R^3\text{ Borel}).$$
For each $f$, $\|G(B)f\|\le\|f\|$, so its values are bounded; indicator
multiplication gives its projection, identity, and intersection laws. Strong
countable additivity follows from dominated convergence applied to $\|f\|^2$.
Its scalar measures are $B\mapsto\int_B\|f(x)\|^2dx$, finite
regular Borel measures on $\mathbb R^3$. On coordinate rectangles,
$$G(C_1\times C_2\times C_3)=E_1(C_1)E_2(C_2)E_3(C_3).$$
The rectangles generate $\mathcal B(\mathbb R^3)$; the published Borel-product
and finite-measure uniqueness theorems show that these rectangle values
uniquely determine the joint PVM ([[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]],
[[lem-finite-measure-uniqueness-on-a-pi-system]],
[[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]): for any two candidate PVMs,
their finite scalar measures agree on the generating rectangles and on the
whole space, so they agree on every Borel set; the polarization identity in
the last lemma then gives equality of the operator values. This constructs the
mathematical joint position PVM; a physical joint detector reading is supplied
only for the finite effect families declared below. For a density operator
$\rho$ define
$\mu^G_\rho(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho G(B))$ for each Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$. Since $G$ is a PVM, this set function is a probability
measure by the general density/PVM calculation used in clause (ii) of P2. For a
finite Borel partition $(B_a)_{a=1}^m$,
the operators $G(B_a)$ are orthogonal projections and sum to $I$. For each
$f\in H_s$,
$\langle G(B_a)f,f\rangle=\|G(B_a)f\|^2\in[0,\|f\|^2]$, so they are
bounded effects with $0\le G(B_a)\le I$ in quadratic-form order. Clause (iv)
of P2 therefore assigns the channel probabilities
$p_a(\rho)=\mu^G_\rho(B_a)$; the two-channel partition
$(B,\mathbb R^3\setminus B)$ assigns $\mu^G_\rho(B)$ to bin $B$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]). Thus $G$ is the
mathematical joint position PVM, while the detector reading used here is the
declared finite-effect model of P2(iv); this does not assert that every three
sharp coordinate measurement is jointly realized by a laboratory apparatus.
For a unit vector $u$, the trace formula for the rank-one operator $P_u$ gives
$$\mu^G_{P_u}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(P_uG(B))=\|G(B)u\|^2=\int_B\|u(x)\|_{\mathbb C^r}^2dx,$$
and P7(iii) leaves identification of this ideal detector with a concrete
apparatus as a tested physical claim with uncertainty.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as required by

[[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Declared two-path assignment.** A **declared two-path preparation model**
of the apparatus is the assignment of two nonzero classes
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\in H_{s}$, called the **path components** of the model with
respect to the declared pair of alternative path conditions of the apparatus,
together with a declared **relative phase** $\varphi\in\mathbb R$ and a declared
**weight** $w\in[0,1]$. The assignment of $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}$, $\varphi$ and
$w$ is part of the preparation model in the sense of clause (i) of P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]): it is declared, not
computed from the framework, and no item of this page asserts that a particle
described by the model "took" one of the two paths.

**(c) Coherent preparation.** The declared two-path model is **admissible at
phase $\varphi$** when $\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\ne0$ in $H_{s}$. When it
is admissible, the **coherent preparation** of relative phase $\varphi$ is the
pure preparation
$$\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi):=\widehat\rho\bigl(\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\bigr),$$
the normalized rank-one density operator defined in clause (a). The relative
phase $\varphi$ is read in radians (dimensionless). Multiplying both path
components by one common nonzero scalar leaves their associated pure density
operator unchanged, while the declared relative phase remains part of the
preparation assignment.

**(d) Incoherent preparation.** For a declared weight $w\in[0,1]$ the
**incoherent preparation**, or **which-path preparation**, of the model is
$$\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w):=w\,\widehat\rho(\psi_{1})+(1-w)\,\widehat\rho(\psi_{2}).$$
It is a density operator: both summands are positive trace-class operators of
trace one; trace-class operators form a vector space, nonnegative real
combinations preserve positivity and self-adjointness, and the trace is linear,
so $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w)=w+(1-w)=1$
([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]],
[[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). The weight $w$
is a declared preparation weight, not an outcome probability.

**(e) Ideal detection bins.** A **declared ideal detector** of the model is a
finite family $\mathcal B=(B_{a})_{a=1}^{m}$ of pairwise disjoint Borel subsets
of $\mathbb R^{3}$ with $\bigcup_{a}B_{a}=\mathbb R^{3}$; the **ideal bin
probabilities** of a preparation $\rho\in D(H_{s})$ are the numbers
$$p_{a}(\rho):=\mu^{G}_{\rho}(B_{a})=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,G(B_{a})\bigr)\qquad(a=1,\dots,m),$$
the reading of the finite-effect clause (iv) of P2 for the declared detector
and its mathematical joint position PVM
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]). By clause (iv) of P2 these numbers are
nonnegative, are at most one, and satisfy
$\sum_{a}p_{a}(\rho)=1$. A single **declared bin** $B$ is the two-element ideal
detector $(B,\mathbb R^{3}\setminus B)$; its probability is $\mu^{G}_{\rho}(B)$.

For the **ideal support**, choose a Lebesgue-measurable representative $f$ of
the unit $L^2$ class and form $S_f:=\{x:\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^r}>0\}$. The
ideal support is the class of $S_f$ under equality up to a Lebesgue-null
symmetric difference. This class is independent of the representative, and
it is not asserted to be a Borel detector bin.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the model data of the pair:
the framework reading, the declared path components and preparations, and the
ideal bin reading of the position observable. They adopt no assumption beyond
P1, P2, P5, P6, P7 and the cited mathematics; the declaration of
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2},\varphi,w$ and of the bins is an apparatus-model input, and
the claim that a concrete two-slit apparatus realizes a particular such
declaration is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7(iii). The
declared bins are subsets of $\mathbb R^{3}$; the model does not claim that a
physical screen of lower dimension is literally a spatial region, and a
marginal, coarse-graining or flux reduction of a state to a screen coordinate
or surface is a separate detection model, not supplied here. No dynamics, no
recorded-event response, no sampling model and no empirical result is
asserted; the recorded-event and sampling models are declared separately on
this page.

Write $\iota_{\mathbb R}:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$ for the canonical-natural map of [[def-canonical-natural]]. If $n\in\mathbb N$ with $n\ge1$ and $z=re^{i\theta}\ne0$, its $n$ distinct roots are
$$r^{1/n}\exp\!\left(i\frac{\theta+2\pi\iota_{\mathbb R}(k)}{\iota_{\mathbb R}(n)}\right),\qquad k\in\mathbb N,\quad 0\le k<n.$$
For $z=0$, the only $n$th root is $0$. Thus the $n$th roots of unity are precisely $\exp\!\left(i\frac{2\pi\iota_{\mathbb R}(k)}{\iota_{\mathbb R}(n)}\right)$ for $k\in\mathbb N$ with $0\le k<n$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[thm-polar-form-with-unique-principal-argument]], [[cor-complex-de-moivre-formula]], [[thm-kernel-and-fibres-of-complex-exponential]], [[thm-nth-roots-exist]], [[def-canonical-natural]], [[def-complex-integer-powers]].

Let $\iota_{\mathbb R}\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$ be the canonical-natural map
of [[def-canonical-natural]], and let $j\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ be the real
embedding $j(x)=x+i0$ from [[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]. For every
$n\in\mathbb N$, the factorial $n!$ is nonzero by
[[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]], so
$\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!)>0$ by [[lem-of-naturals-positive]] and consequently
$j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))\ne0$ in the complex field
[[thm-complex-numbers-form-a-field]].

For $z\in\mathbb C$, define
$$ \exp z:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^n}{j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))}. $$
whenever this complex series converges. Inside a complex expression we
abbreviate the embedded denominator $j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))$ by $n!$, so the
same definition may be written $\exp z=\sum z^n/n!$ without identifying a
natural number with a complex number. Powers and series are those of
[[def-complex-integer-powers]] and
[[def-complex-series-power-series-and-absolute-convergence]]. The convergence
for every $z\in\mathbb C$ is discharged by
[[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]].

For $n\in\mathbb N$ with $n\ge2$, the sum of all $n$th roots of unity is $0$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[thm-complex-nth-roots-and-roots-of-unity]], [[thm-complex-numbers-form-a-field]], [[def-complex-integer-powers]], [[def-monoid-finite-product]], [[thm-generalised-associativity]].

derivations.claim: [Phase-independent normalization] For every $k$, [L1] gives $\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi_{k}}\psi_{2}\|^{2}=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}+2\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi_{1},e^{i\varphi_{k}}\psi_{2}\rangle=N+2\operatorname{Re}\bigl(e^{-i\varphi_{k}}\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle\bigr)=N$, since $\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=0$. This proves (a).

[Root sum] The numbers $e^{i\varphi_{k}}$, $k=0,\dots,n-1$, are exactly the $n$-th roots of unity and $\zeta\mapsto\zeta^{-1}$ permutes them, so $\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}e^{-i\varphi_{k}}=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}e^{i\varphi_{k}}=0$ by [L2].

[Averaged law] By step 1.1 each summand of $\bar p(B)$ has denominator $N$, and by [L1] its numerator is $\int_{B}(\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2})dx+2\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\varphi_{k}}\int_{B}\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle dx)$. Averaging the $n$ summands and using linearity of the finite average, the cross term contributes $\frac{2}{N}\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\bigl(\frac1n\sum_{k}e^{-i\varphi_{k}}\bigr)\int_{B}\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle dx\bigr)=0$ by step 1.2, and the remaining term is $\frac1N\int_{B}(\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2})dx=w_{*}\frac{\int_{B}\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}dx}{\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}}+(1-w_{*})\frac{\int_{B}\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}dx}{\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}}$, since $w_{*}\|\psi_{1}\|^{-2}=N^{-1}=(1-w_{*})\|\psi_{2}\|^{-2}$; this is $\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w_{*})}(B)$ by [L1]. This proves (b) and (c).
